correctness.rationale: For lexicographically ordered binary RM(2,m), N=2^m, m≥3, Q=N/4 and K=1+m+m(m−1)/2. Quadratic polar forms have even rank 2r. The character-sum decomposition makes any nonzero word below weight 3N/8 a weight-Q rank-two quadratic, equivalently the indicator of an affine codimension-two flat. A cyclic window with b>5N/8 zeros confines support to an interval shorter than 3Q/2. Projecting such a flat to the two most significant bits rules out all but four aligned quarter blocks and four neighboring boundary half-quarter blocks, exactly eight length-Q runs with starts multiples of Q/2. Each has a zero gap of length 3Q and hence b-symbol weight b+Q−1 for b≤3Q; all others have full weight. Above b=3Q all nonzero words have full weight, and the strict lower cutoff has extra flats. Dimension K yields coefficients 2^K−9 and 2^K−1. Independently exhaustive Boolean polynomial enumerations for m=3,4,5 at every admissible integer width reproduced complete coefficient tables; the rank/flat argument supplies the all-m proof.
residual_risks: Essential fixed increasing binary-integer coordinate order; arbitrary permutations change b-symbol weights.
Widths b≤5N/8 and polynomial degrees≥3 are outside theorem; finite m verification is supplementary.
